frontmatter.title: Amplifying a known thermal preparation
frontmatter.description: Full-input reflections preserve a postselected thermal purification, with oscillating success and complete measured-trial costs.

children.value: A thermal filter can fail postselection even when its accepted state is accurate. The
supplies an actual preparation unitary, its inverse and a recognizable success pattern. These ingredients let us amplify a

without changing the accepted thermal state. The experiment below checks that preservation, counts the extra access and reflections, and shows why a higher one-attempt success rate need not give a cheaper workload.

Known-input amplitude amplification is implemented with explicit full-register and label-register reflections. The one-qubit Bell-plus-filter example is checked for rounds 0–4, including negative global signs and full coherent source/primitive equivalence. Complete measured trials include initialization, label readout, reference reset and separate X/Z measurements. Degree and temperature bias remain unchanged. Adaptive/fixed-point amplification, certified synthesis, fault-tolerant physical estimates and a Lean proof remain planned.

    proposal = pa.synthesis_conditioning_proposal(check["actual_acceptance_probability"], r)
    workload_rows.append({"rounds":r,"acceptance":check["actual_acceptance_probability"],
                          "source_calls_per_attempt":2*r+1,"accepted_shots_total":workload["total_accepted_shots"],
                          "capped_complete_attempts":workload["worst_case_complete_trials"],
                          "uncapped_expected_complete_attempts":workload["expected_complete_trials"],
                          "hypothetical_coherent_error_allowance":proposal["amplified_coherent_operator_error_allowance"]})
    for axis in ("X","Z"):

        counts = dict(trial.count_ops())
        count_rows.append({"rounds":r,"basis":axis,"wires":trial.num_qubits,"total_instructions":sum(counts.values()),
                           "dependency_depth":trial.depth(),"CX":counts.get("cx",0),
                           "continuous_rotations":sum(counts.get(g,0) for g in ("rx","ry","rz")),
                           "resets":counts.get("reset",0),"measurements":counts.get("measure",0)})
display(pd.DataFrame(count_rows))
display(pd.DataFrame(workload_rows))
